figures.caption: Figure 1: Privileged TFMs pretrained on a GMM-only data prior and equipped with bronze- (empirical dataset-level aggregate statistics), silver- (theoretical model-wise means and variances), and goldgrade (theoretical point-wise mean and variance) PI outperform the baseline (training without PI): (left) they learn faster and reach lower asymptotic loss, with progressively larger gains from bronze to gold relative to the no-PI baseline, and (middle) they achieve strong in-distribution generalization earlier, requiring fewer epochs, thus less data and compute to reach proficiency. (right) PI increases effective depth by freeing ICL capacity: a PIQL’ed 10-layer TFM trained on a mixture of distinct priors (GMM, SCM-S&-M, Copula-D&-P [8]) has linearly probe-able representations for prior type as well as GMM cluster count prediction in earlier layers than a no-PIQL counterpart. (best in color)

Table 2: Comparison of learning paradigms by input source, task structure, and task–input assignment. Our setting uniquely differs from related lines of work in that (1) the additional input, called privileged information (PI) in our case, is not sourced externally but represents internal distribution characteristics derived empirically (meta-features) or theoretically (generator program); (2) the latter, generator-PI is train-time-only while other settings use external input at both training and inference; (3) PI represents given, and not learned, prefix tokens; (4) PI is employed at instance level per dataset, rather than being task-specific; (5) PI enriches the training data in the context by representing distinct yet latent distributions as opposed to different but known tasks.
Table 5: List of the additional LLM-generated meta-features for Meta-PI++.

Figure 2: Training loss (left) and average test AUROC (right) for the proposed PIQL model (red) versus the no-PI baseline (blue). PIQL exhibits accelerated learning, achieving lower loss and higher AUROC in fewer epochs. Despite minor fluctuations during teacher-forcing annealing, PIQL achieves similar loss and performance to the no-transfer variant (gray) at convergence. (best in color)
